_doc: Author dates from English Wikipedia (read 24 Nov 2026) for authors without a usable Pinakes date. 'year' is a sort key (negative = BCE). 'quote' is the sentence the date rests on. Entries with override_pinakes replace a coarser or doubtful Pinakes date (the Pinakes date is still shown on the author page). 'compiler' = dates supplied by Sean Coughlin.

Anthimus.label: fl. 511–534 CE
Anthimus.quote: Anthimus (Greek: Ἄνθιμος; fl. 511–534) was a Byzantine Greek physician at the court of the Ostrogoth king Theodoric the Great

Caelius Aurelianus.label: s. V CE (fl., probably)
Caelius Aurelianus.quote: He probably flourished in the 5th century, although some place him two or even three centuries earlier.

Celsus.label: c. 25 BCE – c. 50 CE
Celsus.quote: Roman physician and encyclopaedist (c. 25 BC - c. 50 AD)

Diocles Carystius.label: s. IV BCE
Diocles Carystius.quote: His significance was as a major thinker, practitioner, and writer of the fourth century.

Marcellus Burdigalensis (Empiricus).label: s. IV–V CE (turn of the centuries)
Marcellus Burdigalensis (Empiricus).quote: a Latin medical writer from Gaul at the turn of the 4th and 5th centuries

Plinius Secundus Iunior.label: early s. IV CE (the compilation)
Plinius Secundus Iunior.quote: The Medicina Plinii or Medical Pliny is an anonymous Latin compilation of medical remedies dating to the early 4th century AD.

Praxagoras.label: born c. 340 BCE
Praxagoras.quote: He was born on the Greek island of Kos in about 340 BC.

Scribonius Largus.label: c. 1 – c. 50 CE
Scribonius Largus.quote: Scribonius Largus Designatianus (c. 1 – c. 50) was the court physician to the Roman emperor Claudius.

Theodorus Priscianus.label: s. IV CE
Theodorus Priscianus.quote: Priscianus was a pupil of the physician Vindicianus, fixing the period of his life in the fourth century.

Apollonius Citiensis.label: fl. c. 60 BCE
Apollonius Citiensis.quote: was a physician (fl. c. 60 BC) belonging to the Empiric school

Aretaeus Cappadox.label: 2nd half of s. II CE (most likely)
Aretaeus Cappadox.quote: most likely lived in the second half of the second century AD

Cassius Felix.label: s. II–III CE (Cassius iatrosophista)
Cassius Felix.quote: an earlier Greek medical writer (2nd or 3rd century AD) [said of Cassius the iatrosophist, author of the Problemata, in the article on the Latin Cassius Felix, fl. 447]

Dioscorides and Ps. Dioscorides Pedanius.label: c. 40–90 CE
Dioscorides and Ps. Dioscorides Pedanius.quote: Born c. 40 AD; Died c. 90 AD

Erotianus.label: s. I CE (reign of Nero, 54–68)
Erotianus.quote: He must have lived (and probably at Rome) in the reign of the emperor Nero (54–68 AD)

Marcellus Sidetes.label: under Hadrian and Antoninus Pius, 117–161 CE
Marcellus Sidetes.quote: lived during the reigns of Hadrian and Antoninus Pius, 117–161 AD

Philumenus.label: in or before s. IV CE
Philumenus.quote: it can only be said that he must have lived in or before the 4th century

Rufus Ephesius.label: c. 70 – c. 110 CE (under Trajan)
Rufus Ephesius.quote: Born c. 70 AD; Died c. 110 AD; he lived in the time of Trajan (98–117)

Soranus Ephesius.label: under Trajan and Hadrian, 98–138 CE
Soranus Ephesius.quote: practiced medicine at Alexandria and Rome in the reigns of Trajan and Hadrian (98–138)

Archigenes Apamensis.label: under Trajan, 98–117 CE
Archigenes Apamensis.quote: he practiced at Rome in the time of Trajan, 98–117
